sections.content: This is a form you will *read*, almost never write. The future subjunctive looks like the *imperfecto de subjuntivo* you know from B1 Unit 4, but ends in *-re*. Take the *ellos* form of the preterite, drop *-ron* and add *-re, -res, -re, -éremos, -ren* (the accent on the stressed vowel keeps *habláremos* apart from the future *hablaremos*): *hablaron* gives *hablare*, *comieron* gives *comiere*, *fueron* gives *fuere*, *tuvieron* gives *tuviere*, *hubieron* gives *hubiere*. It survives in old legal texts, in a few fixed phrases and in proverbs. It is archaic and rare, not wrong. Modern Spanish says the same thing with the present subjunctive or the present indicative.

sections.title: Old form and modern equivalent
rows: El que infringiere el reglamento perderá la parcela.
Whoever breaks the regulation will lose the plot. Modern: El que infrinja… (present subjunctive)
Si alguien no pagare la cuota, perderá la parcela.
If anyone does not pay the fee, he will lose the plot. Modern: Si alguien no paga… (present indicative)
Be that as it may. Modern: Sea lo que sea.
Adonde fueres, haz lo que vieres.
Wherever you go, do what you see done there. (a proverb, still quoted as it is)

items.spanish: Quien infringiere esta disposición será amonestado.
items.english: Whoever breaks this provision will be warned.

items.spanish: Si el socio no cumpliere el plazo, perderá la parcela.
items.english: If the member does not meet the deadline, he will lose the plot.

items.spanish: Sea lo que fuere, el reglamento sigue vigente.
items.english: Be that as it may, the regulation remains in force.

items.spanish: El que hubiere pagado la cuota mantendrá su parcela.
items.english: Whoever has paid the fee will keep his plot.

sections.content: One letter separates three different forms: *hablaré* (future indicative, "I will speak"), *hablare* (the old future subjunctive, no accent) and *hablara* (imperfect subjunctive). Spot the form, then translate it with the modern present: *quien infringiere* is *quien infrinja*. Do not try to use *-re* forms in your own writing.
